description:
Grants the real CI-Server web app (served remotely at http://127.0.0.1:8642 / http://localhost:8642 after the bootstrap page's window.location.replace()) exactly the Tauri IPC it needs to complete native 'Sign in with Companion account': open_external_url_command (launch the OIDC URL in the system browser) and take_pending_deep_link_command (drain a companion://oidc/callback deep link that arrived before the page's listener was up).

TWO grants are required, at two different layers, and missing either one makes the sign-in button silently do nothing:
  * `allow-oidc-ipc` (permissions/allow-oidc-ipc.toml) allows the COMMANDS. Tauri 2 gates app commands reached from a REMOTE origin, not only plugin commands — without this the IPC layer rejects the call before the Rust handler runs, so not even the command's own error logging fires. CI-Hub's desktop shell hit the same wall; see its allow-desktop-ipc.toml.
  * `opener:allow-open-url` allows the opener PLUGIN call INSIDE open_external_url_command, since plugin permissions are checked against the CALLING webview's capabilities.

Narrower than default.json's `opener:default` on purpose: this origin may open a URL and nothing else (no revealItemInDir, no window close/hide/show/focus), and it reaches only these two commands — never start/stop the stack, the docker checks, or the log readers, which belong to the local bootstrap page. That containment is what keeps a future XSS in the product UI from driving the shell.
